title: Variance commentary for the Month 6 management accounts
context: Sophie Grant has to finish the Month 6 (September 2026) variance commentary before Ian Mackie reviews the management accounts. Four lines still say 'TBC' and two have no commentary at all. Ian's month-end chaser email explains the subcontractor issue.
goal: Use Copilot in Excel and Word to analyse the I&E and the repairs cost sheets and draft clear, accurate variance commentary for every material variance.
task_steps: Open the Month 6 management accounts workbook and read the README, which sets out the sign convention and materiality.
Ask Copilot to list every line that has a variance of more than £25,000 or 10%, and check the list against the I&E sheet.
Use the 'Repairs cost by trade' sheet to explain where repairs job costs and subcontractor costs are concentrated.
Draft commentary for the TBC lines, using the month-end chaser email for the Brightline context.
Write a five-bullet executive summary for the Executive Team.
sample_prompts: In the I&E YTD sheet, variances are favourable/(adverse), and for costs, actual below budget is favourable. List every line with a variance over £25,000 or 10% and say whether it is favourable or adverse.
Which trade had the highest job cost from April to September 2026, and how much of the cost was done by subcontractors?
Draft commentary of 2-3 sentences for the subcontractor and damp and mould lines, using the October month-end email from Ian Mackie about the Brightline invoice.
success_criteria: Rent YTD is quoted correctly ({{fact:fin_rent_debit_ytd_m6}}) and described as slightly adverse because of void loss.
In-house pay underspend and subcontractor overspend are explained together, linked to the electrician and plasterer vacancies.
The commentary notes that Brightline invoice BEL-26-0937 is on hold and not accrued.
Shared ownership sales and cost of sales are explained as linked timing variances.
No sign errors: favourable and adverse are used correctly.
trainer_notes: The commentary sheet is part-drafted on purpose. Copilot often gets the sign convention wrong on cost lines, so learners should state it in the prompt (Sophie's tip in the champions chat). The invoice series contains a planted invoice, BEL-26-0937, with no PO or job references. Strong learners will find it in the Invoices library and link it to the subcontractor line. Planned maintenance is favourable because of timing, not a saving.

title: Summarise the Orchard Fields phase 2 appraisal for the Board
module: Copilot in Word and Excel - board reporting
context: The Board wants a one-page summary of the Orchard Fields phase 2 appraisal before its February 2027 decision on phase 3. Tom Lyle has the board-approved appraisal (v3, September 2025), the scheme report, the pipeline data and the October site meeting recap.
goal: Produce an accurate one-page board summary of phase 2's financial case and risks that flags where the appraisal is out of date.
task_steps: Ask Copilot to summarise the appraisal workbook: costs, funding, NPV, IRR and the sensitivity tests.
Compare the appraisal programme with the current completion date in the pipeline report and the site meeting recap.
Identify cost changes that are not in the appraisal (the piling compensation event).
Estimate the direction of the impact using the appraisal's own sensitivity notes.
Draft the one-page summary with a clear 'what has changed since approval' section and a recommendation.
sample_prompts: Summarise this development appraisal for a board audience in 200 words: scheme, costs, grant, NPV, IRR and the key sensitivities.
Compare the practical completion date assumed in the appraisal with the completion date in the development pipeline report and the 22 October site meeting recap. What has changed?
Using the sensitivity notes in the appraisal, explain in plain English what a two-month delay and an extra £160k-£186k of piling cost could do to the NPV.
success_criteria: Quotes NPV £0.42m and IRR 5.9% as the September 2025 figures, not as current.
Spots the programme slip from 30 July 2027 to 30 September 2027 and that the piling cost is missing.
Notes that the sensitivities suggest NPV could fall to around zero or below, so a refreshed appraisal is needed.
Mentions that the Homes England PC milestone forecast has not been updated.
Keeps to one page in board language, with no invented figures.
trainer_notes: Planted inconsistency: the appraisal is the approved version but is out of date (it assumes completion in July 2027, but the pipeline says September 2027, and the piling compensation event is missing). Copilot will report the appraisal figures confidently unless learners ask it to compare sources. Cost +5% on its own turns NPV negative (-£0.31m), and the piling claim is about 1.5% of construction. Learners should not compute a new NPV themselves; they should recommend a refresh, which is an open action for Tom due 30 November.

title: Build an HR handbook Q&A agent
context: Dev Malhotra answers the same handbook questions every week: leave, sickness reporting, flexitime, lone working and standby pay. The People team wants a simple agent, grounded on the Employee Handbook, for staff to use in Teams.
goal: Create a Copilot Studio agent that answers handbook questions accurately, cites the section and sends anything personal or complex to HR.
task_steps: Create an agent and add the Employee Handbook as its only knowledge source.
Write instructions covering tone, citations, scope and escalation.
Test it with at least eight questions, including tricky ones (operatives' summer leave rota, carry-over, sickness reporting for field staff).
Test refusal: ask about a colleague's salary or a disciplinary case.
Improve the instructions based on the test results.
sample_prompts: How many days' annual leave do I get after 6 years?
I'm an operative - how do I report in sick?
Can I take two weeks off in August?
What do I do if I feel unsafe in a resident's home?
success_criteria: Correctly answers leave entitlement ({{fact:ppl_annual_leave}}).
Gives the field staff sickness rule: phone your manager by 08:00 so jobs can be reallocated.
Mentions the operatives' leave limit and the summer rota.
Refuses salary or personal case questions and points to HR.
Cites the handbook section in each answer.
agent_instructions: You are the Silvering Homes HR Handbook helper. Answer questions only from the Employee Handbook. Use plain, friendly UK English and keep answers short. Always say which handbook section your answer comes from. If the handbook doesn't cover the question, say so and suggest contacting the HR Business Partner, Dev Malhotra. Never discuss individual colleagues, salaries, disciplinary or grievance cases, or health information. If someone describes feeling unsafe at work right now, tell them to leave the situation and use the SafeShift SOS button first. Remind users that the full policy applies where it differs from the handbook.
trainer_notes: Good tests: carry-over (5 days, must be used by 30 June) and the out-of-hours standby rates. Show what happens if the agent is also given the People site as knowledge. It may find the overshared pay bands file and reveal named salaries. This links to S-PPL-03 and shows why knowledge sources must be scoped.

title: Write a trades job advert and a 4-week onboarding plan
context: Three electrician campaigns have failed. The recruitment report recommends a shorter advert that leads with what matters to trades, and an onboarding plan that makes new operatives productive within four weeks. The Executive Team has just agreed the market supplement.
goal: Draft a compelling, accurate electrician job advert and a week-by-week onboarding plan for a new electrician.
task_steps: Ask Copilot to read the job description and recruitment report and list what candidates care about.
Draft an advert of no more than 250 words for job boards and social media, with the correct salary and supplement.
Check the supplement amount against the latest decision.
Draft a four-week onboarding plan covering induction, safety, FieldLoop, shadowing, van stock and the lone working app.
Rewrite the advert in a shorter social-media version.
sample_prompts: Using the Electrician job description and the trades recruitment report, write a punchy 250-word job advert aimed at qualified electricians. Lead with pay, van, hours, kit and training.
What market supplement has been agreed for electricians? Check the emails as well as the report.
Create a four-week onboarding plan for a new electrician at the Aylesford depot, as a table by week.
success_criteria: Advert states the £36,000-£39,000 salary plus the £4,500 market supplement (not £3,000).
Includes van, fuel card, 27-30 days' leave, pension and 2391 funding.
Requirements match the JD (18th Edition, AM2, NVQ 3, driving licence).
Onboarding includes lone working, asbestos awareness, safe isolation, FieldLoop and Assure360, and shadowing.
No discriminatory language (for example 'young', 'lads').
trainer_notes: Planted inconsistency: the approved recruitment report says £3,000, but the later ExCo decision in the email thread is £4,500. Copilot grounded only on the report will get it wrong. Daniel's email says 'lads'. Check whether learners copy his tone into the advert.

title: Find the overshared sensitive data before the Copilot pilot expands
context: The Copilot steering group has made a permissions review a condition of expanding the pilot. Three oversharing incidents have been reported. Two of them, a pay file and a Keystone vulnerability export, are still on the People site, even though people believe they have been dealt with.
goal: Use Copilot and SharePoint search to find files with salary or vulnerability data in broadly accessible libraries, judge them against the guidance and write a remediation list.
task_steps: Read the special category data guidance and note the storage rules for each sensitivity label.
Use Copilot (as an ordinary pilot user) to ask questions that might surface salaries or vulnerability information, and note the source files.
Check each file's library, label and contents against the guidance.
Compare what the steering group recap and the champions chat say was done with what is still there.
Write a remediation table: file, location, problem, correct label and location, owner and due date.
sample_prompts: What are the salaries of the electricians at Silvering?
List vulnerable households at Brenchley Gardens.
Which files on the People site contain salary or vulnerability information, and what sensitivity label do they have?
According to the special category data guidance, where should a Keystone export containing vulnerability types be stored and how long should it be kept?
success_criteria: Finds 'Pay Bands and Salaries 2026-27' (Confidential, in Recruitment) and 'Keystone data quality check - vulnerability flags' (Internal, in IT & Data).
Explains why each breaks the guidance: Highly Confidential, restricted library, 30-day retention for exports.
Notices that the steering group actions to move or delete them by 29 October were missed.
Recognises that the Staff Directory is fine (no pay data).
Explains that Copilot did not bypass permissions; the files were stored in the wrong place.
trainer_notes: Planted: two overshared files and missed actions (Craig copied rather than moved the export; Dev's move was blocked by permissions). The Staff Directory is a deliberate control: same source data, but without salary, so it is correctly Internal. Run this on a tenant where the libraries are readable by all staff. Discuss the fix: restricted library, Highly Confidential label, delete the export, and auto-labelling. Never ask learners to open or export the data unnecessarily.
